Pelvic Inflammatory Disease – PID Causes, Symptoms, Diagnosis, Herbal remedies and Ayurvedic Treatment 
 
 
 Introduction 
 
 Herbal Remedies 
 
 
 
 It is most common and serious inflammatory disease in female reproductive tract which is usually caused by sexually transmitted infections (STI). This term is used to describe an infection in lower female reproductive tract that spreads upward to the upper female reproductive system. Lower female reproductive system consists of vagina, cervix and upper female reproductive system consists of uterus, fallopian tubes or uterine tubes and the ovaries. PID affects more than 1 million women each year in U.S. It can be managed with the help of Ayurvedic medicines which are safe and natural. These medicines are purely obtained from herbs like Lodhra (Symplocos racemosa), Neem (Azadirachta indica), Ashok (Saraca indica) and Udumbur (Ficus glomerata). 
 What is Pelvic Inflammatory Disease? 
 Pelvic Inflammatory Disease is commonly called PID is an infection of female reproductive organs. Pelvic inflammatory disease can lead to damage of uterus, fallopian tubes, ovaries and other parts of female genital tract which is primary cause of infertility in women. It occurs when sexually transmitted bacteria enters vagina then spread into uterus, fallopian tubes or ovaries. 
 Pelvic Inflammatory Disease Signs Symptoms 
 Common signs and symptoms of PID may include: 
 
 Fever 
 Painful intercourse 
 Abnormal menstrual bleeding 
 Heavy whitish discharge with unpleasant odor 
 Painful urination 
 Lower abdominal and back pain 
 
 Pelvic Inflammatory Disease Causes 
 PID is infectious disease which may be caused by number of bacteria but most commonly caused by gonorrhea and chlamydia. In normal case, the cervix prevents the entry of bacteria into other internal reproductive organs but in case of sexually transmitted disease the cervix itself gets infected and less able to prevent the entry of bacteria. About 90% of cases are because of gonorrhea and chlamydia which spread during unprotected sex. 
 Other causes include abortion, childbirth and pelvic procedures. 
 Complications Associated with PID 
 If pelvic inflammatory disease is left untreated then it causes severe problems like damage of reproductive organs and accumulation of infected fluid in fallopian tubes. 
 Some complications may include: 
 
 Ectopic (tubal) pregnancy 
 Infertility 
 Severe pelvic pain 
 
 Pelvic Inflammatory Disease Diagnosis 
 Doctor may diagnose PID on the basis of signs and symptoms, a pelvic examination, analysis of vaginal discharge or urine tests. 
 There are some tests to diagnose the bacteria in vaginal fluid: 
 
 Pelvic examination – In this test doctor uses a cotton swab to take sample from vagina and cervix for analysis of organism that causes infection. 
 Ultrasound – It helps to create the images of reproductive organs. 
 Biopsy (endometrial) – small piece of Endometrium (inner lining) is taken for testing. 
 Laparoscopy – It helps to view pelvic organs for diagnosis.
